title: The Headlines About Cannabis and Diabetes Vs The Details
description: The headlines today scream “Type 2 Diabetes Risk Quadruples for Cannabis Users, Large Study Finds”. And, yes, that’s what the study says. The artic...
content_html_sanitized:
The headlines today scream “Type 2 Diabetes Risk Quadruples for Cannabis Users, Large Study Finds”. And, yes, that’s what the study says. The article linked above is a very complete report.

 

However, as it also reports, “During the study period, 2.2% of cannabis users developed diabetes, compared with just 0.6% of non-users. This meant cannabis users had nearly four times the risk of type 2 diabetes.”

 

Now, that is not an insignificant number, because cannabis is used by millions of people in Europe and North America, and around the world.However, from an individual's perspective, it is hardly a major health concern. It is easy to get a large percentage difference from a very small number.

 

Also, correlation is not causation, especially not from a very small number. Headline: “Almost 98% of cannabis users don’t have diabetes!!”?? Not likely.

 

However, I have been trying to raise a different question. To what degree is the correlation between cannabis use and various health problems the result of attempted self-medication? In other words, did cannabis use cause diabetes, or did diabetes cause the cannabis use?

 

The attempt at self medication may even have been counterproductive, but why should anyone believe the medical profession that has denied that it has any medical benefit?

See

The New York Post Can’t Figure Out Why Pregnant Women Use Cannabis. Perhaps Because They Are Not Getting Adequate Medical Care?

And

The Paradox of Cannabis Self Medication

 

Of course, to the government funded “scientific research” industry looking for problems associated with cannabis, correlation looks like causation.

See  

Scientific fraud has become an 'industry,'alarming analysis finds

And

McCaffrey Threatens Lockyer With Arrest If California Does Research On Medical Marijuana, But Says "A Massive Research Effort" Is Needed To See If Marijuana Has Any Medical Value; New Stalling Begins -- 3 Articles
